newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Handlowy may open above PLN 40 - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Handlowy may open above PLN 40 - analysts.

text.p: Bank Handlowy SA, Poland's largest commercial bank in terms of capital, could start trade on the main market of the Warsaw bourse on Monday above 40 zlotys, or soon stabilise there, analysts said.

The 9.75 million-share retail tranche of the bank's May-June public offering at 35 zlotys each was three times subscribed and the 19.5-million-share institutional tranche was 17.4 times subscribed with foreign demand over $3.5 billion.
The 24-percent long-term investor tranche went to JP Morgan, Zurich Insurance and Swedbank.

But analysts said profit-taking could soon begin as some players accumulate funds to invest in copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA, whose public offering worth over one billion zlotys starts on Monday. KGHM starts bourse trade on July 10.

"More interesting than the debut is how (Handlowy) will look on the second or third day; it could have a pop on day one even to 40-42 zlotys and then might go down to the end of the KGHM subscription," said Ryszard Wojnowski of PBI brokerage. @

Analysts said Handlowy's IPO oversubscription was a good sign and that next week's peak or even debut price could pierce 45 zlotys, near the price of the firm's GDR currently trading in London at around $14.2.
But they doubted the bank had the numbers for its stock to shine in the medium term, with Polish banks slumping this year in part due to increased obligatory reserve requirements.

"It (Handlowy) shouldn't really be valued much more than 35 zlotys a share or 1.4 times 1996 book value...It's good against other banks but it's fully valued against its profitability," said Andreas Wesemann, an analyst at ING Barings in London.

During the first five months this year Handlowy's net profit fell to 38.4 million zlotys from 60 million zlotys in the same period last year. At the end of last year the bank had own funds of 1.85 billion zlotys.

Analysts said that in the longer term the market price of Handlowy, which specialises in trade finance and corporate lending, could depend on the costs of its expected expansion of retail banking by increasing its network of over 40 branches.
It also plans to accelerate investment banking, another area promising high growth and better-than-average returns.

"It's unlikely any of the Polish banks are making returns on their investment banking activities of 40 or 50 percent and we would not expect (Handlowy) to be able to do that for quite some time either," said Salomon Brothers' Matthew Czepliewicz.
"Nevertheless we would not want to see an ROE dilution from moving into investment banking," he said.
